topic: Which purpose-of-payment codes should Egypt use — ISO 20022 vs a national list
question: Are the ten codes proposed for Egypt real, and does Egypt publish its own list?
answer_short: Six of ten were real ISO 20022 codes; four (TRVL, RDEV, ITSV, TRAI) were invented and must be replaced. Egypt publishes no purpose-code list that could be found, and adopted ISO 20022 on 2026-06-21, so the ISO family is the right choice.
verified: SUPP, SCVE, SALA, BEXP, CHAR, RENT and GDDS are real ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose1Code values. SUPP=Supplier Payment · SCVE=Purchase & Sale of Services · SALA=Salary Payment · BEXP=Business Expenses · CHAR=Charity Payment · RENT=Rent · GDDS=Purchase & Sale of Goods. OTHR=Other exists as the explicit catch-all.

TRVL, RDEV, ITSV and TRAI are NOT ISO 20022 purpose codes. They do not appear in the official External Purpose Codes list (125 codes) nor in LHV's independent reference. There is no ISO code for research and development, for IT/telecom services as a purpose, or for training — the nearest real ones are SCVE for services, STDY for study, NWCH for network charge, and OTHR as catch-all.

The Central Bank of Egypt adopted ISO 20022 for interbank SWIFT messaging effective 2026-06-21, and the Egyptian RTGS has been upgraded to comply. This makes the ISO 20022 purpose-code family the correct one for Egypt rather than a national numeric list like Jordan's or India's.

No published Central Bank of Egypt purpose-of-payment CODE list was found. Searches across CBE, Citi and trade sources returned the ISO 20022 migration but no Egypt-specific code table. Consistent with the Citi notice, which asks for a DESCRIPTION and gives narrative examples rather than codes.
refuted: Egypt requires a national purpose-of-payment code list comparable to Jordan's CBJ codes or India's RBI codes. No such published list was found, and the bank's own notice asks for a free-text description instead.
collateral_finding: UNESCO already runs a non-ISO code in production: T015L PH3 is 'TRVL Travel & Tour Expenses' for the Philippines, and TRVL is not an ISO 20022 purpose code. So the existing configuration is not uniformly standards-based — worth knowing before citing the Philippines as the ISO precedent.
